headline: The Sahm recession indicator has crossed its conventional threshold.
what_changed: Evaluation month 2024-12-01: three-month average 4.50% versus a prior 12-month low of 4.00% (gap 0.50 percentage points). Published 0.50 threshold met: True.
why_it_matters: The Sahm rule measures how far the three-month average unemployment rate has risen above its recent low. It is associated with recessions already under way in US history. It is not an NBER recession call, a guaranteed forward forecast, or a market-timing rule.
historical_context: The Sahm rule was proposed by Claudia Sahm as a real-time recession indicator based on labour-market deterioration. Aqil applies the published arithmetic only; this run does not claim an academic replication certificate or a validated point-in-time historical study.
investor_implications: For a long-horizon investor, this is one labour-market signal to monitor alongside inflation, policy and portfolio goals. Economic conditions, market pricing, asset allocation and specific trades remain distinct. Investment implication from the engine: no_action. Market pricing assessed here: unknown.
confidence_and_limitations: Data sufficiency: sufficient. Analysis mode: latest_revised. These rows are labelled latest-revised retrospective data from BLS. They reflect values published today, not what was known at an earlier decision date. They must not be used for genuine point-in-time backtests until independently archived provider vintages exist. Verification: unverified. Publication allowed: False. Evidence: publication gate remains fail-closed, this assessment is not claim or span verification.
what_comes_next: Monitor the monthly BLS employment situation release for revised unemployment rates. Related measures include payroll growth and participation; they are not substituted here.

assumptions: US seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate in percent.
Three-month average uses the evaluation month and the two prior months.
Prior low uses the minimum three-month average over the 12 months before the evaluation month.
The 12-month look-back excludes the evaluation month (Claudia Sahm, 2019).
Threshold is 0.50 percentage points (Published Sahm rule threshold (0.50 percentage points)).
limitations: This is a published association with recessions already under way, not an NBER determination.
Not a forward recession forecast or an investment signal.
Market pricing is not assessed here.
